# Agent rules v2 — from 2026-10-18 (git tag `agent-rules-v2`)

Version: v2. Base: everything in `v1.md` applies unless changed below. To roll back, write `v1` into `CURRENT` and brief agents with
"rules v1" (or `git checkout agent-rules-v1 -- .notes/agent_rules`). Do not edit this file once tagged; changes → `v3.md`.

## Changes vs v1

### Orchestrator
1. **Parallelism 2–3 agents** (was up to 5) — fewer queue waits on the build/GPU locks and a quota pace that lasts to the weekly reset.
   Raise only when the weekly quota is clearly ahead of schedule (check `get_usage` after every landing).
2. **Smaller tasks**: one finding / one function family per agent; no "and also" tails. Follow-ups found by an agent become new briefs.
3. Every brief starts with: `Rules: .notes/agent_rules/v2.md` (agents read it first) and names the agent's worktree.

### Every agent
4. **Context cap (continuation hand-off)**: when your context reaches ~200k tokens (or after ~150 tool calls), stop at the next clean
   point: commit what is done, write `.notes/reports/<ID>-state.md` (what's done with commits, what's in progress with exact files and
   next steps, open hypotheses with evidence, scratch paths), and finish with a hand-back that says `CONTINUE: <ID>-state.md`. The
   orchestrator then starts a fresh continuation agent from that file. Never let a context grow toward 500k+.
5. **One helper sub-agent at a time, only for read-heavy self-contained jobs** that return a short answer, e.g.:
   - asm-vs-source comparison of one function ("disassemble 0xADDR, compare with File.cpp:Func, list every deviation"),
   - crash-stack / large-log analysis ("from log X find the first anomaly before the crash, ≤ 20 lines"),
   - the mandatory line-by-line review pass of your own port against the asm,
   - mechanical generation from a given template (e.g. oracle rows for a listed set of functions).
   Use `general-purpose` on `model: sonnet`, give it a complete brief (paths, addresses, expected output format, "≤ N lines"), no
   builds/game runs/commits by the helper (read-only + scratch files), and never more than one helper at a time. Don't delegate
   work that needs what you already learned — that pays twice.
6. **Fast test runs**: use the run-build test switches when available — no-vsync (`NOTSA_STANDALONE_NOVSYNC=1`, run build only; the
   vsync-locked Present costs ~78 ms/frame on this PC → 30–75 s cold starts vs ~2 s), windowed 960x600, videos skipped — unless the
   bug is about exactly that behaviour; frame-time measurements always state the mode.
7. **Compile cache**: when the compile cache is set up (see docs/WINDOWS_SETUP.md), configure your worktree with it so a fresh
   worktree doesn't rebuild 1200 TUs from scratch.
8. Builds/tests always `run_in_background` (already a v1 addendum, now a rule); `build_locked.sh` handles dead holders.
